newsitem.title: ITALY: Ultra-mini ultra stylish at Gucci.
newsitem.headline: Ultra-mini ultra stylish at Gucci.

text.p: Ultra miniskirts and mannish wide-shouldered suits cut a clean and seductive profile in the autumn/winter 1997/98 collection of luxury Italian fashion house Gucci on Thursday.

Designer Tom Ford took pinstripes for women's suits and cut angular, wide-shouldered but slender backed jackets, exploiting traditionally masculine lines and materials to bring out the slimmer form of the female inside them.
Black and blue pinstripe trousers were wide-legged and loose at the hip where they were cut low over the bone and held up with thin black patent leather belts slung across the stomach.

Suit jackets were fastened with concealed buttons, some cut like a double-breasted suit but then buttoned further than normal across the body to give a kimono appearance, or drawn in at the waist by wide, shiny black leather belts.

Suit jackets were lengthened into short dresses, one with a bck vent which was worn over a black polo-neck sweater, while pinstripes served for pencil skirts also cut low at the hip and worn with knee-high black patent leather boots.

Knitwear included sheer wool jerseys in dark hues and angled wraparound mini dresses with long sleeves, while leather wear was black with neat, short-cropped jackets, some tightly waisted then flared over the hip and worn over tight mid-thigh minis.

Then came ultra-minis, one cut with the simple, straight tightness of a Hollywood-style loincloth, split wide up one thigh, and worn with a shiny black leather belt and black jersey, while a second was a wraparound dress with a deliberately uneven join.
Another innovation included ski pants in monotone black, hard scarlet, green and flesh tone which were angled over one hip and worn with sheer, sequinned tops of the same hue.

For elegant evening wear, models wore long, narrow matt black shoulderless gowns with shiny leather trim at the chest and neck. One dress had a reverse halter collar, leaving the chest free and instead crossing high over the shoulder blades.
For those cold winter nights came outsize fur jackets in lemon, red, black or baby blue worn over glittering jersey dresses and all stopping dramatically mid-thigh.
The Milan shows continue on Friday with German Jil Sander, top Italian designer Gianfranco Ferre, design duo Domenico Dolce and Stefano Gabbana and fashion house Prada.
